intent: Show a Command list in a modal dialog above the page, with a visually hidden title and description naming it.
typical_uses: A command palette the application opens from a keyboard shortcut or a button

dont_use_when.situation: The searchable list sits inside the page or a panel, not in an overlay
A modal window holding a form, a confirmation or other content that is not a searchable list

invariants.text: `open` and `defaultOpen` are both accepted; `defaultOpen` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `open` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.

The children are rendered inside a Command root the component creates itself, with no props other than its class, so the root's `label`, `filter`, `shouldFilter`, `value`, `loop` and `vimBindings` cannot be set here; the search input's `aria-labelledby` points at that root's hidden label, which is empty.

`title` and `description` render as a visually hidden heading and paragraph where CommandDialog sits in the tree, outside the portalled popup and whether or not the dialog is open; the dialog takes its accessible name and description from them.
`className` is merged onto the popup, which command.module.css sets to no padding and no gap and, from 640px wide, a maximum width of 40rem.

Escape and a press outside the popup close the dialog, reporting the reason to `onOpenChange`; with nested dialogs open, only the topmost one closes. `disablePointerDismissal` keeps an outside press from closing it.

anti_patterns.dont: Wrap the children in a Command of your own
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass CommandInput and CommandList directly; CommandDialog already renders the Command root, and a second one makes the inner parts read the inner root while the outer one filters nothing

a11y.by: command.test.tsx asserts role="dialog" named "Command Palette" by default and "Quick actions" with a custom `title`, no "Close" button by default, and that Escape closes the dialog

children.states: children is the palette's content, React nodes holding CommandInput and CommandList
children.because: `React.ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more; the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

title.states: title is the dialog's accessible name, rendered visually hidden
title.because: `React.ReactNode` is a union, and the compiler emits one JSON type per property. Defaults to "Command Palette".

description.states: description is the dialog's accessible description, rendered visually hidden
description.because: `React.ReactNode` is a union, and the compiler emits one JSON type per property. Defaults to "Search for a command to run...".

modal.states: modal is true (the default), false, or "trap-focus" to trap focus without locking page scroll or outside pointer interaction
modal.because: `boolean | 'trap-focus'` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so a boolean-or-string union is left unasserted.

onOpenChange.states: onOpenChange is a callback called with the next open state and event details, not a value
onOpenChange.because: `(open: boolean, eventDetails) => void`; the second argument carries Base UI's change-event details, including the reason (such as a trigger press, an outside press or Escape). No JSON Schema type covers a function.

onOpenChangeComplete.states: onOpenChangeComplete is a callback called with the open state once the open or close animation has finished
onOpenChangeComplete.because: `(open: boolean) => void` - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

actionsRef.states: actionsRef is a ref the dialog fills with imperative `close` and `unmount` actions
actionsRef.because: `React.RefObject<DialogRootActions | null>` - a ref object holding functions, which no JSON Schema type covers.

handle.states: handle is an opaque object from the primitive's Dialog.createHandle(), shared with a trigger placed outside this dialog
handle.because: `DialogHandle<unknown>` is a class instance holding the dialog's store, not data; the kit re-exports no createHandle, so a caller imports it from the primitive.

triggerId.states: triggerId is the id of the trigger a controlled dialog is open for, or null
triggerId.because: `string | null` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so a string-or-null union is left unasserted.

defaultTriggerId.states: defaultTriggerId is the id of the trigger an initially open dialog is open for, or null
defaultTriggerId.because: `string | null` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so a string-or-null union is left unasserted.

unexposed_parts.reason: Rendered fixed and visually hidden to carry `title` and `description`; the caller sets their text only through those two props.
The popup the list renders in; only its `className` and `showCloseButton` reach it through this component's own props.
Created by the component around its children with no configurable props (see children-inside-its-own-command).

good.title: A palette the caller opens and closes
good.code:
<CommandDialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} title="Quick actions">
  <CommandInput placeholder="Type a command or search..." />
  <CommandList>
    <CommandEmpty>No results found.</CommandEmpty>
    <CommandItem value="new-file" onSelect={() => setOpen(false)}>New file</CommandItem>
  </CommandList>
</CommandDialog>

bad.title: Command props passed to the dialog
bad.why: CommandDialog takes Dialog's root props, not Command's; `shouldFilter` and `loop` are never passed to the Command it renders, so the list still filters and does not wrap.

capabilities.description: Default false: when true, DialogContent renders its close (X) button in the popup.
